task: Add a single project-owned playthrough runner that owns the whole preview-server lifecycle, and expose one stable npm script per scenario.
notes: Today each scripts/playthrough-*.mjs expects a caller to have already built the app and started `vite preview` on some port, then be handed a URL and an output-path PREFIX. That makes every acceptance run a manual three-step coordination, and it scatters screenshots as sibling files with ad-hoc prefixes. One runner should own the lifecycle instead, and each run should leave a bounded, self-describing set of artifacts. Do not change any scenario script's own logic, checks or screenshot names - only how it is launched and where its output prefix points.
requirements: Add scripts/playthrough-run.mjs: a runner taking one scenario name as its first argument (e.g. `node scripts/playthrough-run.mjs zoo`).

It maps a scenario name to its existing scenario script via an explicit table in the runner: restaurant -> scripts/playthrough.mjs, drink-stand -> scripts/playthrough-drink.mjs, zoo -> scripts/playthrough-zoo.mjs, coloring -> scripts/playthrough-coloring.mjs, sports -> scripts/playthrough-sports.mjs. An unknown name exits 2 listing the valid names.

Lifecycle, owned end to end by the runner: choose a free TCP port; spawn `vite preview` on it (via the local node_modules/.bin binary, not a global one); poll the URL until it answers or a bounded timeout (~30s) elapses; run the scenario; always terminate the preview process in a finally block, including on error, on a failing scenario, and on SIGINT/SIGTERM.
If dist/ is missing or empty the runner exits nonzero with a one-line message telling the caller to run `npm run build` first. It must NOT build implicitly.

Artifacts are bounded to the current run: before running, the runner removes and recreates .tmp/playthrough/<scenario>/ and passes the scenario script an output prefix inside that directory (the scenario scripts already append their own `-NN-name.png` suffixes to the prefix they are given).

After the scenario finishes, the runner writes .tmp/playthrough/<scenario>/manifest.json containing at least: scenario, command, startedAt, endedAt, durationSeconds, exitCode, passed (boolean), url, and screenshots (an array of paths relative to the repository root, sorted, for THIS run only). It also prints the screenshot list to stdout as a short block - never a directory listing of anything wider than this run's own folder.

Exit status is the scenario's status: 0 only when the scenario exited 0. A scenario failure, a preview that never became ready, a missing dist/, or an internal runner error must all exit nonzero. The manifest is still written when the scenario ran and failed.
Output must be bounded: stream the scenario's own stdout/stderr through, but the runner's own chatter is at most a handful of lines (port chosen, waiting, scenario exit, screenshot block).

Add npm scripts to package.json: `playthrough` (the generic runner, so `npm run playthrough -- zoo` works) plus `playthrough:restaurant`, `playthrough:drink-stand`, `playthrough:zoo`, `playthrough:coloring`, `playthrough:sports`, each invoking the runner with its scenario name.
Add `.tmp/` to .gitignore if it is not already ignored.
constraints: Do NOT modify any existing scripts/playthrough*.mjs scenario file, and do not change their checks, selectors, timings or screenshot names.
Do NOT add any new dependency. `playwright` is already a local devDependency of this project and must stay the only browser framework - do not add @playwright/test, puppeteer, or anything else.
Do NOT modify src/, index.html, vite.config.js, SPEC.md, or anything under src/minigames/ - other work is in flight there.
Use only Node built-ins in the runner (node:child_process, node:net, node:fs, node:path, node:url). No shell chaining, no `npx`.
Resolve the vite binary from this project's own node_modules; never rely on a binary above the project root.
Write the runner with an editor, not by shelling out a heredoc or a Python rewrite.
startingPoints: package.json - existing scripts: dev, build, preview, test
scripts/playthrough-zoo.mjs - read its argv handling (URL, output prefix) to confirm the prefix contract
scripts/playthrough.mjs - the restaurant scenario, same argv contract

behavioralAcceptance.notes: Launching a real browser is not available in the delegated execution environment, so the controller performs this acceptance after implementation. Do not attempt it and do not report the runner as proven.
